samples.summary: Slides toolbar gains a Remove-link button, but the canonical slides toolbar design doc is not updated — the rationale is filed in the *docs* font-controls doc instead. `slides-toolbar-redesign.md:254` still describes the slides text-edit cluster as "B / I / U, Color, Link … rendered with `showStrikethrough={false}` and `showHighlight={false}`", and :260 repeats the same flag list for the mobile Format sheet; neither mentions `showRemoveLink`. The repo files design docs by subsystem (folding into the canonical subsystem doc), so a slides-surface decision documented only in `docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md` § "Removing a link on slides" leaves the slides doc stale and the decision hard to find from the slides side.

Scope beyond the issue: the originating task (#1051, docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-clear-formatting-keeps-links-todo.md) plans five items, all inside packages/docs plus one design-doc and test update; none of its acceptance criteria mention a new toolbar control. This change additionally adds a shared `showRemoveLink` prop, a new unlink button, an optional `removeLink` on the shared `TextFormattingEditor` interface, and wires two slides surfaces (desktop text-edit section + mobile Format sheet). The gap it fills is real (slides has no link popover), but it is unrequested UI scope that should at least be acknowledged as a follow-on rather than folded in silently.

samples.summary: The pending-style design doc, which is the canonical record of the collapsed-caret rule, still specifies step 4 as `pending.set(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, cursor.position)` flat. This change adds a real exception to that rule (a trailing-edge `href: undefined` re-arm, in both `TextEditor.clearFormatting` and `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting`), documented only in `docs-font-controls.md`. The subsystem doc that owns pending-style semantics is left stale/contradictory.

The trailing-edge re-arm *rule* is now hand-copied in two places even though the *predicate* was shared: `editor.ts:3362-3372` and `text-editor.ts:3439-3448` each recompute `exitsLink` (isAtLinkTrailingEdge || prior pending href===undefined) and each build `{ ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, href: undefined }`. The task's own lessons file names "sharing the list is not sharing the rule" as the failure mode that caused the review miss here; leaving two copies of the rule invites the same drift (e.g. a future third entry point, or the slides text-box path, silently omitting it).

`removeLink?()` is declared optional on the shared `TextFormattingEditor` and called as `editor.removeLink?.()`, so any surface that opts into `showRemoveLink` without implementing it renders a visibly-enabled button that silently does nothing. Both current implementers (docs `EditorAPI`, slides `SlidesTextBoxEditor`) have the method, so a required member — or gating the button on its presence — would encode the contract instead of failing quietly.

Same gap the slides button was added for may remain on the docs header/footer surface: the slim header/footer toolbar deliberately renders no link controls ("no lists, no link, no styles dropdown"), and `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` explicitly supports carets in headers/footers, so a run there can carry an `href` (autolink-on-space in the shared TextEditor) while Clear formatting no longer drops it. If the docs link popover does not surface in header/footer editing, there is now no reachable way to remove such a link — the exact reasoning used to justify the slides button was not applied here.

samples.summary: Acceptance criterion "same behaviour in the slides text-box editor" is met only for range selections: `TextBoxEditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` routes through an `applyStyleImpl` that returns early when there is no selection (text-box-editor.ts:820), so a collapsed-caret clear is a no-op there while both docs entry points stage a pending style (and now a link exit). The divergence predates this change, but this change is where the collapsed-caret rule was defined, and the shared contract comment claims parity.
